name: Tāraka-yoga
method_summary: Meditation on the 'crossing' light between the brows through the three targets and the voids, proceeding from tāraka with form to tāraka without form and to the mind-less (amanaska) state.
prerequisites: renouncer endowed with the six qualities (Advayatāraka)

name: Contemplation of the three targets (lakṣya-traya)
method_summary: Attending to the inner target (kuṇḍalinī, inner sound, blue light), the outer target (colours and lights in space) and the intermediate target (voids).
signs_of_progress: lights, stars, a diamond mirror, the full moon, the midday sun, a flame (Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa 2.1)

name: Śāmbhavī mudrā
method_summary: Gazing with open, unblinking eyes while attention rests on the inner target; three forms by the eyes' opening (amā, pratipat, pūrṇimā), the open 'full-moon' gaze being recommended.
signs_of_progress: the place where such a yogin lives is purified (Advayatāraka)

name: Vaiṣṇavī mudrā
method_summary: The inner target held while the gaze is outward and unblinking (Śāṇḍilya 1.31); in the Nādabindu, the seal held while listening to the inner sound in the right ear.

name: Closing the senses (ṣaṇmukhī)
method_summary: Closing ears, eyes and other openings with the fingers so that the inner sounds are heard.

name: Attention to the inner sound (nādānusandhāna)
method_summary: Seated in siddhāsana, attention is held on the inner sound in the right ear; the sounds pass from loud (ocean, cloud, drum) to subtle (bells, flute, vīṇā, bee); the mind follows the subtlest until it dissolves with it.
signs_of_progress: body like a log, unaware of heat and cold, gaze, breath and mind steady (Nādabindu 52–56)

name: Ajapā-japa (the haṃsa / so'ham breath-mantra)
method_summary: Awareness of the breath's natural sound — 'ha' out, 'sa' in, 21,600 times a day — and its reversal as 'so'ham' ('I am He').

name: Meditation on Oṃ (praṇava)
method_summary: Contemplation and repetition of Oṃ through its measures to the half-measure and the soundless; Oṃ as bow, chariot or fire-stick; also joined with breath-regulation.
signs_of_progress: Brahman shines within twelve months for one who repeats 12,000 praṇavas daily (Sannyāsa 2.103–104)

name: Purification of the channels (nāḍī-śodhana)
method_summary: Alternate-nostril breathing in regular sessions to purify the channels, or purification by knowledge of the Self (Darśana 5). Counts and schedules given by the texts are not reproduced.
signs_of_progress: lightness, radiance, stronger digestive fire, leanness, inner sound manifest (Yogatattva 44–45; Yogacūḍāmaṇi 98–99)

warnings.text: Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.
Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.

name: Kevala-kumbhaka (retention without inhalation or exhalation)
method_summary: The spontaneous suspension of breath that arises after long practice; the Yoga Upaniṣads associate it with awakening of kuṇḍalinī and with powers. Summary only.

warnings.text: Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.
Powers that arise must not be displayed.

name: Sahita-kumbhaka (sūryabheda, ujjāyī, śītalī, bhastrī)
method_summary: Retention joined with inhalation and exhalation, in four named varieties (Yogakuṇḍalī 1.19ff.). Summary only; no counts.

warnings.text: Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.

name: The three locks (mūla, uḍḍīyāna, jālandhara)
method_summary: Root, abdominal and throat locks applied with breath-practice to turn the breaths upward and keep them in the suṣumnā.

name: Mahāmudrā
method_summary: The 'great seal' named among the haṭha practices of the Yogatattva and Dhyānabindu; recorded by name and purpose only.

name: Mahābandha and mahāvedha
method_summary: Combined locks and the 'great piercing' named in the Yogatattva; summary only.

name: Viparītakaraṇī (the inverted practice)
method_summary: An inverted posture-seal named in the Yogatattva; the text warns that the practitioner must then eat sufficiently or the fire consumes the body.

warnings.text: The practitioner must eat plenty, otherwise the fire quickly consumes the body.

name: Khecarī mudrā
method_summary: The 'moving in space' seal of the tongue, taught as a secret vidyā with a mantra (melana) received from the guru's mouth; the bodily procedures described by the texts are not reproduced. Also given inner meanings (the gaze; the renouncer's 'mudrā').

warnings.text: Learn only from a guru who knows it from text, meaning and practice; keep it secret.
Proceed gradually, never all at once, or the body perishes.

name: Vajrolī, amarolī, sahajolī
method_summary: Named in the Yogatattva among haṭha practices concerned with retaining bindu; recorded by name only.

warnings.text: Union with women causes loss of bindu; the yogin should avoid their company.

name: Śakticālana (moving the power)
method_summary: Rousing the kuṇḍalinī from her place and leading her upward through the suṣumnā, with sarasvatī-cālana; the texts say it removes abdominal disease. Summary only.

name: The five element concentrations (pañca-dhāraṇā)
method_summary: Holding breath and mind in five regions of the body, each with its element, shape, colour, seed-syllable and deity (Brahmā, Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva; in the Triśikhi the four vyūhas and Vāsudeva); each conquers its element. Durations omitted.
signs_of_progress: mastery of the element: not harmed by earth, water, fire, air; moving in space (Yogatattva 83–102)

name: Five kinds of withdrawal (pratyāhāra)
method_summary: Forcibly withdrawing the senses; seeing all that is seen as the Self; offering the fruits of acts; turning from all objects; and moving/holding the breath through the eighteen vital points (Darśana 7; Śāṇḍilya 1.69); the Yogatattva's withdrawal is regarding all perceived as the Self.

name: Concentration on the eighteen vital points (marma)
method_summary: Holding breath and attention successively at eighteen vital points from the toes upward and back (Triśikhi 128–133; Darśana 7; Śāṇḍilya 1.69).

name: The 'razor' concentration (kṣurikā)
method_summary: A concentration that 'cuts' through the vital points and channels with mind and breath; summary only.

name: Meditation with and without qualities
method_summary: Meditation on a form (the Lord in the heart, Maheśvara as oneself) or on the Self's nature without form, leading to samādhi (Yogatattva 104; Śāṇḍilya 1.71; Darśana 9).

name: Meditation in the heart lotus
method_summary: Seated in solitude, body straight, meditating on the Lord (with Umā; or as the thumb-sized Oṃ; or as the flame) in the heart lotus (Kaivalya 5–7; Dhyānabindu 19; Vāsudeva).

name: Inner worship mapped onto the state beyond mind
method_summary: Each service of worship understood as a moment of the mind-less state — invocation as abandoning action, the lamp as the sun of consciousness, salutation as 'so'ham', praise as silence (Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa 2.2).

name: Contemplation of the body as the Śrīcakra
method_summary: The body's openings, channels, winds and faculties contemplated as the enclosures and deities of the Śrīcakra; worship as contemplation of non-difference (Bhāvanā; Tripurā).

name: The breath fire-offering (prāṇāgnihotra)
method_summary: Before eating, food is sprinkled with mantras and offered in five oblations to the five breaths; the body is the sacrificial ground.

name: The renunciation rite (saṃnyāsa-dīkṣā)
method_summary: Penances, śrāddhas (including for oneself), the virajā homa, placing the fires in oneself, the declaration of renunciation said three times, the gift of fearlessness, abandoning topknot and thread (or not, in the Vaiṣṇava rite), receiving staff and cloth, and the teaching of praṇava and great saying.
prerequisites: dispassion; the fourfold means; eligibility; consent of kin (varies by text)

name: Alms in the bee's way (mādhukarī)
method_summary: Taking a little food from several houses after the household cooking fires are out, never from a single house; eating moderately (half food, a quarter water, a quarter air).

name: Wandering (pārivrājya) and the rains retreat
method_summary: Wandering alone or with one companion; one night in a village, five in a town, seven at a sacred place; staying in one place during the four rainy months; dwelling in empty houses, temples, tree-roots, caves.

name: Contemplating the body's impurity
method_summary: Reflecting on the body as a compound of bones, flesh, blood and impurities to loosen attachment (Nāradaparivrājaka 3; Maitreya 2).

name: Self-inquiry ('who am I?')
method_summary: Inquiring 'who am I, how did this world arise?' (Yogakuṇḍalī 3.27–29), and discriminating Self from not-Self (Tejobindu 5).

name: Breath-control as knowledge
method_summary: Exhalation as negating the world or renouncing objects, inhalation as 'I am Brahman' or scriptural knowledge, retention as steadiness in realization (Tejobindu 1.31–33; Varāha 5.58).

name: Moderate diet (mitāhāra)
method_summary: Sweet, unctuous food eaten leaving a quarter of the stomach empty; avoiding the hot, sour, salty, pungent; wholesome milk, ghee, wheat, mung, rice; called the chief of the yamas (Yogatattva 28–29, 46–49; Yogacūḍāmaṇi 43).

name: Postures of the Yoga Upaniṣads
method_summary: Lists vary: four chief postures (siddha, padma, siṃha, bhadra — Yogatattva, Dhyānabindu); eight (Śāṇḍilya); nine (Darśana); eleven (Varāha); seventeen (Triśikhi); siddhāsana and padmāsana are pre-eminent.

name: Three kinds of japa
method_summary: Loud, whispered (upāṃśu) and mental recitation, each far superior to the previous (Darśana 2; Śāṇḍilya 1.2).

name: Saṃyamas for powers (Śāṇḍilya)
method_summary: Concentration on parts of the body, on merit and demerit, on the throat, the kūrma-nāḍī, the light in the head and so on, each yielding a power.

name: Tripuṇḍra (three lines of ash)
method_summary: Ash taken with the five brahma-mantras and applied in three horizontal lines, each line standing for a fire, a letter of Oṃ, a guṇa, a world, a power, a Veda and a deity (Kālāgnirudra); for all four stages of life.

name: Bathing in sacred ash (bhasma-snāna)
method_summary: Smearing the whole body with ash prepared with mantras (Bṛhajjābāla; Bhasmajābāla; Atharvaśiras).

name: The pāśupata vow
method_summary: Taking ash with 'fire is ash, wind is ash…' and smearing the body, for release of the paśu from its bonds (Atharvaśiras 5).

name: Wearing rudrākṣa beads
method_summary: Wearing beads of chosen size, colour and number of faces, consecrated with mantras, observing food and conduct rules (Rudrākṣajābāla).

name: Ūrdhvapuṇḍra (vertical Vaiṣṇava mark)
method_summary: Vertical marks of gopīcandana clay applied with mantras at twelve places (householder) or fewer (students, forest-dwellers, ascetics; the paramahaṃsa one on the forehead) (Vāsudeva).

name: Consecrating the rosary (akṣamālā)
method_summary: Choosing bead material, threading with gold, silver and copper threads, and invoking the fifty letters a–kṣa into the beads (Akṣamālikā).

name: Recitation of the Śatarudrīya
method_summary: Recitation of the Rudra hymn of the Yajurveda; 'these are the names of immortality' (Jābāla 3); by it one becomes atyāśramin and reaches kaivalya (Kaivalya 2).

name: Recitation of Śiva mantras
method_summary: Recitation of Śiva's five- or six-syllable mantra and of Dakṣiṇāmūrti's mantras (Pañcabrahma; Bhasmajābāla; Dakṣiṇāmūrti).

name: Recitation of the eight-syllable Nārāyaṇa mantra
method_summary: Recitation of 'oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya', which leads to Vaikuṇṭha and is the tāraka (Nārāyaṇa; Tārasāra; Ātmabodha).

name: Recitation of the Rāma tāraka mantra
method_summary: Recitation of Rāma's mantra, the tāraka given at Avimukta (Rāmatāpanī; Rāmarahasya).

name: Recitation of the Gopāla mantra
method_summary: Worship and recitation of Kṛṣṇa's five-part mantra with meditation on his form (Gopālapūrvatāpanī).

name: Recitation of the Narasiṃha mantra-king
method_summary: The anuṣṭubh 'king of mantras' of Narasiṃha, by which Prajāpati creates (Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanī; Avyakta).

name: Recitation of the sixteen names
method_summary: Repeating 'hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare, hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare'; the Kalisantaraṇa says no rule binds it, and that three and a half crore repetitions free from the gravest sins.
notes: Gauḍīya practice recites it with the 'hare kṛṣṇa' half first; the Upaniṣad gives the 'hare rāma' half first.

name: The Cākṣuṣmatī vidyā
method_summary: Praise of the Sun for health of the eyes; one who knows it has no eye disease and none in his family is blind (Akṣi 1).
